key_insight: The paper proposes a topology-driven, non-parametric way to estimate which 3D medical foundation models will transfer best for segmentation, using graph-based alignment instead of costly fine-tuning.
clinical_relevance: This could help medical imaging teams choose segmentation models faster and more efficiently for diverse anatomical tasks, especially when compute is limited.
method: Uses Minimum Spanning Trees (MSTs) to compare dense voxel features with semantic labels.
Measures transferability with two scales: Local Boundary-Aware Topological Consistency (LBTC) and Global Representation Topology Divergence (GRTD).
Combines the two scores with a task-adaptive gating mechanism; a randomly initialized decoder is used as a spatial projector to stabilize distance estimates.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 114,000 3D medical volumes across multiple anatomical tasks, the method improved average weighted Kendall performance by 0.36 and was reported to be 56× faster than exhaustive fine-tuning.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on topology and graph construction from dense features, performance may vary with feature quality, decoder setup, and dataset-specific anatomy/annotation complexity.
paper_title: Topology-Driven Transferability Estimation for 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models
